multiRename.title: Multi-rename

@multiRename.title.description: Title of the Multi-Rename Tool sheet (Ctrl+M), which renames many files at once with a name mask, like Total Commander's tool of the same name.

@multiRename.nameMask.description: Label of the field holding the rename mask for the file name: plain text plus placeholders in brackets such as [N] (old name) or [C] (counter).

@multiRename.extensionMask.description: Label of the field holding the rename mask for the file extension, kept separate so a typo can't break the file type. [E] keeps the old extension.

@multiRename.insertPlaceholder.description: Accessible name of the row of buttons that insert a placeholder such as [N] or [C] into the name mask at the caret.

@multiRename.search.description: Label of the search field of the rename tool's search & replace. Supports * and ? wildcards and a|b|c lists.

@multiRename.replace.description: Label of the replacement field of the rename tool's search & replace. With a list search, x|y|z pairs up with it.

@multiRename.caseSensitive.description: Search & replace option: only match the same uppercase/lowercase letters.

@multiRename.firstOnly.description: Search & replace option: replace only the first match in each name, not all of them.

@multiRename.includeExtension.description: Search & replace option: also search and replace in the file extension.

@multiRename.regex.description: Search & replace option: the search is a regular expression; $1, $2 in the replacement insert its groups.

@multiRename.substitute.description: Search & replace option: when the search matches, the whole name becomes the replacement (Total Commander's "Subst.").

@multiRename.searchOptions.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, the accessible name of the row of small toggle chips beside the search fields that turn the search options on and off (Match case, First match only, Include extension, Regular expression, Replace whole name).

@multiRename.searchOptionHelp.setup.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, each search option (Match case, First match only, Include extension, Regular expression, Replace whole name) is a small toggle chip beside the search fields. Its tooltip names the option, shows its keyboard shortcut, and gives a tiny worked example: a replace on a made-up file name, with the result when the option is on and when it's off. This line sets up the example: what is searched for, what replaces it, and the file name it runs on. Keep the <code> tags around the three placeholders: they show in a code font.

placeholders.name: a made-up file name (e.g. Photo photo.jpg)

@multiRename.searchOptionHelp.on.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, each search option (Match case, First match only, Include extension, Regular expression, Replace whole name) is a small toggle chip beside the search fields. Its tooltip names the option, shows its keyboard shortcut, and gives a tiny worked example: a replace on a made-up file name, with the result when the option is on and when it's off. Labels the line showing the new name with the option turned on. Keep it as short as possible.

@multiRename.searchOptionHelp.off.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, each search option (Match case, First match only, Include extension, Regular expression, Replace whole name) is a small toggle chip beside the search fields. Its tooltip names the option, shows its keyboard shortcut, and gives a tiny worked example: a replace on a made-up file name, with the result when the option is on and when it's off. Labels the line showing the new name with the option turned off. Keep it as short as possible.

@multiRename.case.description: Label of the menu that changes the letter case of the new names, applied after search & replace.

@multiRename.case.unchanged.description: Letter-case menu option: keep the letter case as it is.

@multiRename.case.lower.description: Letter-case menu option: all letters lowercase. Written in lowercase on purpose, to show the result.

@multiRename.case.upper.description: Letter-case menu option: all letters uppercase. Written in uppercase on purpose, to show the result.

@multiRename.case.firstUpper.description: Letter-case menu option: the first letter of the name uppercase, the rest lowercase.

@multiRename.case.words.description: Letter-case menu option: the first letter of every word uppercase, the rest lowercase. Written that way on purpose, to show the result.

@multiRename.removeDiacritics.description: Option: turn letters with accents and other diacritics into plain letters (á becomes a, ž becomes z, ß becomes ss), in every language.

@multiRename.greekToLatin.description: Checkbox that writes Greek letters in Latin ones, the way Greek passports do (ELOT 743): Αθήνα becomes Athina.

@multiRename.normalizeUnicode.description: Checkbox that renames names whose accented letters are stored as a letter plus a separate accent mark (as macOS and network drives often store them) to the single-character form Windows, Linux, and websites expect. The names look the same before and after.

multiRename.presets.title: Presets

@multiRename.presets.title.description: Label of the button at the bottom left of the Multi-rename tool that opens the menu of presets (saved rename settings), and the accessible name of that menu. Followed by a down arrow and, when one is loaded, the preset's name.

@multiRename.presets.edited.description: Shown on the Presets button after the loaded preset's name once the user changed a field, so the fields no longer match the preset. {preset} is the preset's name.

@multiRename.presets.tooltip.description: Tooltip of the Presets button in the Multi-rename tool. The keyboard shortcut (F2) is shown beside it.

@multiRename.presets.saved.description: Heading of the presets the user saved, at the top of the Presets menu (above the presets that come with Cmdr).

@multiRename.presets.reset.description: Presets menu item that sets every field back to its starting value, so all names stay as they are (Total Commander's <Default>).

@multiRename.presets.saveAs.description: Presets menu item that asks for a name and saves the tool's current fields as a new preset. The ellipsis means it asks for more before acting.

@multiRename.presets.rename.description: Item in a saved preset's submenu that asks for a new name for that preset.

@multiRename.presets.update.description: Item in a saved preset's submenu that overwrites that preset with the tool's current fields. Greyed out when the preset already matches them.

@multiRename.presets.delete.description: Item in a saved preset's submenu that deletes that preset. Only the preset goes; no files are touched.

@multiRename.presets.saveTitle.description: Accessible name of the small popup that asks for a name to save the current fields as a preset (opened with Cmd+S or Save current as…).

@multiRename.presets.renameTitle.description: Accessible name of the small popup that asks for a new name for a saved preset.

@multiRename.presets.save.description: Button in the save-preset popup that saves the current fields under the typed name.

@multiRename.presets.renameConfirm.description: Button in the rename-preset popup that gives the preset the typed name. Renames the preset only, never files.

multiRename.presets.clash: There’s already a preset called “{preset}”. Replace it?

@multiRename.presets.clash.description: Shown in the preset-name popup when the typed name belongs to another saved preset. Pressing Enter again or the Replace button replaces that preset. {preset} is its name.

@multiRename.presets.replace.description: Button in the preset-name popup, after the question whether to replace the preset that already has the name. Replaces that preset.

@multiRename.preset.removeDiacritics.description: Built-in preset that keeps names as they are but removes diacritics (á becomes a, ž becomes z).

@multiRename.preset.greekToLatin.description: Built-in preset that writes Greek letters in Latin ones (Αθήνα becomes Athina) and changes nothing else.

@multiRename.preset.normalizeUnicode.description: Built-in preset that only stores accented letters in the single-character form Windows, Linux, and websites expect; the names look the same.

@multiRename.presetName.description: Label of the name field in the small popup that saves the current fields as a preset (Cmd+S) or renames a saved one.

@multiRename.preview.description: Accessible name of the table that previews every file's old and new name.

@multiRename.oldName.description: Preview table column: the file's current name.

@multiRename.newName.description: Preview table column: the name the file will get.

@multiRename.statusColumn.description: Header of the preview list's status column, read out by screen readers only: the column shows a small symbol on each row with a problem (invalid name, duplicate, name taken, gone), and nothing on rows that are ready or unchanged.

@multiRename.status.unchanged.description: Preview note: the new name is the same as the old one, so the file is left alone.

@multiRename.status.duplicate.description: Preview note: another file in this batch would get the same new name, so neither is renamed.

@multiRename.status.targetExists.description: Preview note: a file that stays in the folder already has this name.

@multiRename.status.invalidName.description: Preview note: the new name can't be a file name (empty, too long, or "." / "..").

@multiRename.status.disallowedCharacter.description: Preview note: the new name contains a character file names can't have, such as a slash. {character} is that character.

multiRename.error.unclosed: A placeholder is missing its closing “]”

@multiRename.error.unclosed.description: Shown when a mask has a [ without a matching ].

@multiRename.error.unknown.description: Shown when a mask has a placeholder that doesn't exist. {placeholder} is what's between the brackets.

@multiRename.error.badRegex.description: Shown when the search is a regular expression that can't be parsed.

multiRename.error.gone: This folder isn’t open any more. Close Multi-rename and open it again.

@multiRename.error.gone.description: Shown when the pane the tool renames in moved to another folder.

multiRename.error.nothingToRename: Nothing to rename: every new name is the same as the old one or has a problem

@multiRename.error.nothingToRename.description: Shown when Rename is pressed but no file is ready to be renamed.

multiRename.error.notConnected: This location isn’t connected right now

@multiRename.error.notConnected.description: Shown when the drive or server of the folder is no longer connected.

multiRename.error.couldntStart: Couldn’t start renaming. Try again in a moment.

@multiRename.error.couldntStart.description: Shown when the rename couldn't start (the rename queue refused it, or something went wrong inside Cmdr). Nothing was renamed.

multiRename.error.timedOut: That took too long, so Cmdr stopped waiting. Try again, or select fewer files.

@multiRename.error.timedOut.description: Shown under the Multi-rename preview when working out the new names, or getting the rename ready after Start, took longer than Cmdr waits. Nothing was renamed. 'Cmdr' is the app name; keep it untranslated.

multiRename.summary: {ready, plural, one {# to rename} other {# to rename}} · {unchanged, plural, one {# unchanged} other {# unchanged}} · <problemsToggle>{problems, plural, one {# problem} other {# problems}}</problemsToggle>

@multiRename.summary.description: Footer summary of the Multi-rename preview: how many files will be renamed, how many keep their name, and how many have a problem. While there are problems, the part inside <problemsToggle> is a link-styled toggle button: pressing it shows only the files with a problem in the preview list, pressing it again shows every file. Keep the <problemsToggle> tags around the problem count.

placeholders.ready: how many files get a new name
placeholders.unchanged: how many files keep their name
placeholders.problems: how many files can’t be renamed (invalid name, duplicate, name taken, gone)

@multiRename.cancel.description: Button that closes the tool without renaming.

@multiRename.undo.description: Footer button that reverses the last multi-rename of this session (all its files at once). It sits beside Cancel (multiRename.cancel), so the two must read differently.

multiRename.undoTooltip: {count, plural, one {Renames # file back to its old name} other {Renames # files back to their old names}}

@multiRename.undoTooltip.description: Tooltip of the Undo button. {count} is how many files the last multi-rename renamed.

multiRename.undoStarted: {count, plural, one {Renaming # file back} other {Renaming # files back}}.

@multiRename.undoStarted.description: Toast after Undo started reversing the last multi-rename. {count} is how many files.

@multiRename.results.description: Footer link (Total Commander’s name) that opens the list of old and new names in the user’s text editor, so they can edit the new names by hand.

multiRename.results.editing: Edit the new names in your text editor and save the file. They show here when you come back to this window.

@multiRename.results.editing.description: Shown under the sheet’s fields while the names list is open in the text editor. Each line is an old name, a tab, and the new name.

multiRename.results.edited: {count, plural, one {# name comes from your edited list} other {# names come from your edited list}}.

@multiRename.results.edited.description: Shown under the sheet’s fields when the preview uses names the user typed in the text editor (Results). {count} is how many files carry such a name.

@multiRename.results.readNow.description: Link that reads the edited names list back right away, instead of waiting for the user to come back to the window.

@multiRename.results.discard.description: Link that drops the names typed in the text editor, so every file shows the name the settings give it.

multiRename.results.gone: The names list is gone. Open Results again to write a new one.

@multiRename.results.gone.description: Shown when the edited names list can’t be read back (it was deleted or moved).

multiRename.error.couldntWriteNames: Couldn’t write the names list. Check that your startup disk has free space.

@multiRename.error.couldntWriteNames.description: Shown when Results couldn’t create its text file in the temporary folder.

multiRename.resultsTooltip: Edit the new names in your text editor, then come back here

@multiRename.resultsTooltip.description: Tooltip of the Results footer link (multiRename.results): it opens the list of old and new names in the user's text editor, one file per line, to change any new name by hand; the sheet reads the list back when the user returns to the window.

multiRename.editedName: You typed this name in Results

@multiRename.editedName.description: Tooltip and screen-reader text of a small pencil mark beside a row of the preview whose new name the user typed by hand in the Results list (multiRename.results) rather than one the settings made.

@multiRename.rename.description: Primary button that renames the files that are ready. {count} is how many.

multiRename.started: {count, plural, one {Renaming # file} other {Renaming # files}}. You can roll it back from the operation log.

@multiRename.started.description: Toast after Rename starts. {count} is how many files. The operation log is the window listing past operations, where Undo is. "Roll back" is the button's name in the operation log (operationLog.dialog.rollBack): use the same words.

multiRename.error.previewOutOfDate: The folder changed since the preview. Check the new preview, then rename again.

@multiRename.error.previewOutOfDate.description: Shown when Rename is pressed but files in the folder changed after the preview was shown, so nothing was renamed and the preview is refreshed.

multiRename.error.readOnly: This folder can’t be renamed in: it’s inside an archive or another read-only place

@multiRename.error.readOnly.description: Shown when Rename is pressed in a folder that can't be changed, such as the inside of a zip archive.

@multiRename.status.missing.description: Preview note: a file the user picked for renaming was deleted or moved out of the folder while the tool was open, so it can't be renamed.

@multiRename.status.ready.description: Screen-reader text in the preview's status column for a file that will be renamed. Sighted users see no mark on these rows; only the problem rows get a symbol.

multiRename.reason.duplicate: Another file in this batch gets the same new name, so neither is renamed.

@multiRename.reason.duplicate.description: Tooltip on the preview's duplicate symbol: the full reason behind multiRename.status.duplicate.

multiRename.reason.targetExists: A file that stays in this folder already has this name, so this one keeps its name.

@multiRename.reason.targetExists.description: Tooltip on the preview's "name is taken" symbol: the full reason behind multiRename.status.targetExists. The file that holds the name isn't part of the rename (or can't be renamed itself).

multiRename.reason.missing: This file was moved or deleted after Multi-rename opened, so it’s left out.

@multiRename.reason.missing.description: Tooltip on the preview's "gone" symbol: the full reason behind multiRename.status.missing. "Multi-rename" is the tool's name; match multiRename.title.

@multiRename.reason.empty.description: Tooltip on the preview's "not a valid name" symbol when the masks produce an empty name.

multiRename.reason.tooLong: The new name is too long for a file name.

@multiRename.reason.tooLong.description: Tooltip on the preview's "not a valid name" symbol when the new name is longer than a file name may be.

@multiRename.reason.reserved.description: Tooltip on the preview's "not a valid name" symbol when the new name is "." or "..", which name a folder itself and its parent. Keep both dot names exactly as they are.

@multiRename.reason.disallowedCharacter.description: Tooltip on the preview's "not a valid name" symbol when the new name holds a character file names can't have, such as a slash. {character} is that character.

multiRename.selectionChanged: The folder changed while Multi-rename was opening. Check your selection, then try again.

@multiRename.selectionChanged.description: Warning toast when ⌃M (Multi-rename) didn't open because files appeared or disappeared in the folder at that moment, so the selected rows may no longer be the files the user picked. Nothing was renamed.

multiRename.swapsSkipped: {count, plural, one {Skipped # rename that swaps names} other {Skipped # renames that swap names}}. Rename those files one at a time.

@multiRename.swapsSkipped.description: Warning toast after Rename starts on cloud storage (S3), when some renames swap names with each other (for example a → b and b → a). On S3, renaming a folder copies everything inside it, and copying one folder onto another that is still there would mix their contents, so those renames were skipped and the files kept their names. {count} is how many (always 2 or more). Match the wording of askCmdr.renameUndo.swapsSkipped.

@multiRename.archiveTitle.description: Alert title when ⌃M (Multi-rename) is pressed while browsing inside a zip archive. Cmdr can rename files in a zip one by one, but the Multi-rename tool only works in folders on a drive. "Multi-rename" is the tool’s name; match multiRename.title.

multiRename.archiveMessage: To rename files in this zip, rename them one at a time.

@multiRename.archiveMessage.description: Alert body under multiRename.archiveTitle. Points the user to renaming files inside the zip one by one (the regular single-file rename), which does work there.

@multiRename.counterEditor.marker.description: Accessible name (read by screen readers) of the small ▾ button drawn right after each counter placeholder [C] in the Multi-rename mask field. Clicking it opens a popover that edits one counter placeholder ([C], or [C10+5:3] with its own start, step, and digits) in the Multi-rename name or extension mask. It opens from a small ▾ after the placeholder, or with the down arrow key while the text cursor is in it. A VERB phrase.

multiRename.counterEditor.title: Counter

@multiRename.counterEditor.title.description: Accessible name of the small popover that edits one counter placeholder ([C], or [C10+5:3] with its own start, step, and digits) in the Multi-rename name or extension mask. It opens from a small ▾ after the placeholder, or with the down arrow key while the text cursor is in it. A NOUN: the counter that numbers the renamed files.

@multiRename.counterEditor.start.description: Label of the number field in the small popover that edits one counter placeholder ([C], or [C10+5:3] with its own start, step, and digits) in the Multi-rename name or extension mask. It opens from a small ▾ after the placeholder, or with the down arrow key while the text cursor is in it: the number the first file gets. A NOUN (where counting starts), not a verb.

@multiRename.counterEditor.step.description: Label of the number field in the small popover that edits one counter placeholder ([C], or [C10+5:3] with its own start, step, and digits) in the Multi-rename name or extension mask. It opens from a small ▾ after the placeholder, or with the down arrow key while the text cursor is in it: how much the number goes up per file (down, when negative). A NOUN.

@multiRename.counterEditor.digits.description: Label of the number field in the small popover that edits one counter placeholder ([C], or [C10+5:3] with its own start, step, and digits) in the Multi-rename name or extension mask. It opens from a small ▾ after the placeholder, or with the down arrow key while the text cursor is in it: how many digits the number has at least; shorter numbers get leading zeros (3 digits turns 7 into 007). A NOUN.

@multiRename.counterEditor.counts.description: Plain-language line under the fields of the small popover that edits one counter placeholder ([C], or [C10+5:3] with its own start, step, and digits) in the Multi-rename name or extension mask. It opens from a small ▾ under the placeholder, when the text cursor rests in it, or when the mouse rests on it. Shows the first three numbers the counter gives, exactly as they appear in the new names (with leading zeros when the counter has more digits).

placeholders.first: the first file’s number as it appears in the name (e.g. 1, or 001)
placeholders.second: the second file’s number as it appears in the name (e.g. 3, or 003)
placeholders.third: the third file’s number as it appears in the name (e.g. 5, or 005)

multiRename.placeholderHelp.name: The file’s name, without its extension

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.name.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, a tooltip on a placeholder button (such as [N], [E], or [C]) explains what that placeholder puts in the new name, lists a few of its other forms, and shows each with an example on a made-up file (Beach day.jpg, in the folder Trips/Lisbon 2026, last changed 2026-07-14 09:05:30). What the [N] placeholder stands for. A noun phrase.

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.extension.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, a tooltip on a placeholder button (such as [N], [E], or [C]) explains what that placeholder puts in the new name, lists a few of its other forms, and shows each with an example on a made-up file (Beach day.jpg, in the folder Trips/Lisbon 2026, last changed 2026-07-14 09:05:30). What the [E] placeholder stands for, for example “pdf”. A noun phrase.

multiRename.placeholderHelp.parent: The name of the folder the file is in

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.parent.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, a tooltip on a placeholder button (such as [N], [E], or [C]) explains what that placeholder puts in the new name, lists a few of its other forms, and shows each with an example on a made-up file (Beach day.jpg, in the folder Trips/Lisbon 2026, last changed 2026-07-14 09:05:30). What the [P] placeholder stands for. A noun phrase.

multiRename.placeholderHelp.counter: A number that goes up by one step per file, in the list’s order

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.counter.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, a tooltip on a placeholder button (such as [N], [E], or [C]) explains what that placeholder puts in the new name, lists a few of its other forms, and shows each with an example on a made-up file (Beach day.jpg, in the folder Trips/Lisbon 2026, last changed 2026-07-14 09:05:30). What the [C] counter placeholder stands for. A noun phrase.

multiRename.placeholderHelp.date: The date the file was last changed: year, month, and day

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.date.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, a tooltip on a placeholder button (such as [N], [E], or [C]) explains what that placeholder puts in the new name, lists a few of its other forms, and shows each with an example on a made-up file (Beach day.jpg, in the folder Trips/Lisbon 2026, last changed 2026-07-14 09:05:30). What the [YMD] placeholder stands for (the modification date, as 20261009). A noun phrase.

multiRename.placeholderHelp.time: The time the file was last changed: hours, minutes, and seconds

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.time.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, a tooltip on a placeholder button (such as [N], [E], or [C]) explains what that placeholder puts in the new name, lists a few of its other forms, and shows each with an example on a made-up file (Beach day.jpg, in the folder Trips/Lisbon 2026, last changed 2026-07-14 09:05:30). What the [hms] placeholder stands for (the modification time, as 143207). A noun phrase.

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.oneChar.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, a tooltip on a placeholder button (such as [N], [E], or [C]) explains what that placeholder puts in the new name, lists a few of its other forms, and shows each with an example on a made-up file (Beach day.jpg, in the folder Trips/Lisbon 2026, last changed 2026-07-14 09:05:30). Meaning of a form like [N3]: only that one character of the name. Positions count from 1.

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.charRange.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, a tooltip on a placeholder button (such as [N], [E], or [C]) explains what that placeholder puts in the new name, lists a few of its other forms, and shows each with an example on a made-up file (Beach day.jpg, in the folder Trips/Lisbon 2026, last changed 2026-07-14 09:05:30). Meaning of a form like [N2-5]: that run of characters, both ends included. Positions count from 1.

multiRename.placeholderHelp.lastChars: {count, plural, one {The last character} other {The last # characters}}

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.lastChars.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, a tooltip on a placeholder button (such as [N], [E], or [C]) explains what that placeholder puts in the new name, lists a few of its other forms, and shows each with an example on a made-up file (Beach day.jpg, in the folder Trips/Lisbon 2026, last changed 2026-07-14 09:05:30). Meaning of a form like [N-3-]: the last few characters, counted from the end.

placeholders.count: how many characters from the end (e.g. 3)

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.firstChar.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, a tooltip on a placeholder button (such as [N], [E], or [C]) explains what that placeholder puts in the new name, lists a few of its other forms, and shows each with an example on a made-up file (Beach day.jpg, in the folder Trips/Lisbon 2026, last changed 2026-07-14 09:05:30). Meaning of a form like [E1]: only the first character.

multiRename.placeholderHelp.firstChars: {count, plural, one {The first character} other {The first # characters}}

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.firstChars.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, a tooltip on a placeholder button (such as [N], [E], or [C]) explains what that placeholder puts in the new name, lists a few of its other forms, and shows each with an example on a made-up file (Beach day.jpg, in the folder Trips/Lisbon 2026, last changed 2026-07-14 09:05:30). Meaning of a form like [P1-3]: the first few characters.

placeholders.count: how many characters from the start (e.g. 3)

multiRename.placeholderHelp.grandparent: The name of the folder above that one

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.grandparent.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, a tooltip on a placeholder button (such as [N], [E], or [C]) explains what that placeholder puts in the new name, lists a few of its other forms, and shows each with an example on a made-up file (Beach day.jpg, in the folder Trips/Lisbon 2026, last changed 2026-07-14 09:05:30). Meaning of [G]: the folder that holds the file’s folder (the grandparent folder). A noun phrase.

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.counterStar.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, a tooltip on a placeholder button (such as [N], [E], or [C]) explains what that placeholder puts in the new name, lists a few of its other forms, and shows each with an example on a made-up file (Beach day.jpg, in the folder Trips/Lisbon 2026, last changed 2026-07-14 09:05:30). Meaning of a counter form like [C10]: the first file gets this number.

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.counterStep.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, a tooltip on a placeholder button (such as [N], [E], or [C]) explains what that placeholder puts in the new name, lists a few of its other forms, and shows each with an example on a made-up file (Beach day.jpg, in the folder Trips/Lisbon 2026, last changed 2026-07-14 09:05:30). Meaning of a counter form like [C+5]: how much the number grows per file.

placeholders.step: how much the number grows per file (e.g. 5)

multiRename.placeholderHelp.counterDigit: {digits, plural, one {At least # digit} other {At least # digits}}, with leading zeros

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.counterDigi.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, a tooltip on a placeholder button (such as [N], [E], or [C]) explains what that placeholder puts in the new name, lists a few of its other forms, and shows each with an example on a made-up file (Beach day.jpg, in the folder Trips/Lisbon 2026, last changed 2026-07-14 09:05:30). Meaning of a counter form like [C:3]: numbers get leading zeros up to this width (7 becomes 007).

multiRename.placeholderHelp.counterAll: All three at once; a minus step counts down

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.counterAll.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, a tooltip on a placeholder button (such as [N], [E], or [C]) explains what that placeholder puts in the new name, lists a few of its other forms, and shows each with an example on a made-up file (Beach day.jpg, in the folder Trips/Lisbon 2026, last changed 2026-07-14 09:05:30). multiRename.placeholderHelp.datePart: The day alone; [Y] and [M] work the same way
